lesson_scope: Volumes of revolution about the x-axis for regions with inner and outer boundaries (washers), subtractive cylinder formulations, changing radial rules, and regions enclosed between two curves.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rotating region between two horizontal lines to form a hollow tube.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of the washer method formula V = pi * int(y_outer^2 - y_inner^2 dx).

hints: Recall the washer method formula for rotation about the $x$-axis: $V = \pi \int_a^b (y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2) \, dx$.

walkthrough.text:
State the washer method volume formula for rotation about the $x$-axis:
$$V = \pi \int_a^b \left(y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2\right) \, dx$$

Identify outer and inner radii and compute the difference of squares:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 3 \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 9$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = 1 \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 1$$
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 9 - 1 = 8$$

Integrate across the interval $[0, 4]$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^4 8 \, dx = \pi [8x]_0^4 = \pi (8(4) - 0) = 32\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rotating region between horizontal line y = 2 and y = x.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of washer method with outer cylinder minus inner cone.

hints: For $x \in [0, 2]$, the line $y = 2$ lies above $y = x$, so $y_{\text{outer}} = 2$ and $y_{\text{inner}} = x$.
Set up and evaluate: $V = \pi \int_0^2 (4 - x^2) \, dx = \pi \left[4x - \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \pi \left(8 - \dfrac{8}{3}\right) = \dfrac{16}{3}\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify outer and inner boundaries on $[0, 2]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 2, \quad y_{\text{inner}} = x$$

Form the difference of squares for the integrand:
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 2^2 - x^2 = 4 - x^2$$

Evaluate the definite integral from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^2 (4 - x^2) \, dx = \pi \left[4x - \frac{1}{3}x^3\right]_0^2 = \pi \left(8 - \frac{8}{3} - 0\right) = \frac{16}{3}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies outer radius $2$ and inner radius $x$, setting up $\pi \int_0^2 (4 - x^2) \, dx = \pi \left[4x - \frac{1}{3}x^3\right]_0^2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rotating region between y = sqrt(x) and y = x^2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of washer method between two intersecting power curves.

hints: Square each function individually: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 = (\sqrt{x})^2 = x$ and $y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x^2)^2 = x^4$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine outer and inner curves on $[0, 1]$ and square each:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = \sqrt{x} \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = x$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = x^2 \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x^4$$

Set up the washer integral on $[0, 1]$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^1 \left(y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2\right) \, dx = \pi \int_0^1 (x - x^4) \, dx$$

Integrate and substitute the limits:
$$= \pi \left[\frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^5}{5}\right]_0^1 = \pi \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{5} - 0\right) = \pi \left(\frac{5 - 2}{10}\right) = \frac{3}{10}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies $y_1^2 - y_2^2 = x - x^4$ and integrates $\pi \left[\frac{1}{2}x^2 - \frac{1}{5}x^5\right]_0^1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rotating region between y = 2x and y = 1 on [1, 2].

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of washer method with non-zero lower bound.

hints: Square both expressions: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 4x^2$ and $y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 1$, giving $y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 4x^2 - 1$.

walkthrough.text:
Square the outer and inner functions on $[1, 2]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 2x \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 4x^2$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = 1 \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 1$$

Set up the integral for the hollow solid from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$:
$$V = \pi \int_1^2 (4x^2 - 1) \, dx = \pi \left[\frac{4}{3}x^3 - x\right]_1^2$$

Substitute the limits:
$$= \pi \left(\left(\frac{4(8)}{3} - 2\right) - \left(\frac{4(1)}{3} - 1\right)\right) = \pi \left(\left(\frac{32}{3} - \frac{6}{3}\right) - \left(\frac{4}{3} - \frac{3}{3}\right)\right)$$
$$= \pi \left(\frac{26}{3} - \frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{25}{3}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rotating region between constant line and reciprocal curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of washer method with negative power integrand.

walkthrough.text:
Square the outer and inner boundaries on $[1, 2]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 2 \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 4$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = \frac{1}{x} = x^{-1} \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x^{-2}$$

Set up and evaluate the washer integral:
$$V = \pi \int_1^2 (4 - x^{-2}) \, dx = \pi \left[4x - \frac{x^{-1}}{-1}\right]_1^2 = \pi \left[4x + \frac{1}{x}\right]_1^2$$

Substitute the limits:
$$= \pi \left(\left(4(2) + \frac{1}{2}\right) - \left(4(1) + \frac{1}{1}\right)\right) = \pi \left(\left(8 + \frac{1}{2}\right) - 5\right) = \pi \left(\frac{17}{2} - \frac{10}{2}\right) = \frac{7}{2}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: rotating region between radical curve y = sqrt(x+2) and y = 1.

hints: Square each boundary: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 = x + 2$ and $y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 1$, giving $y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x + 2) - 1 = x + 1$.

walkthrough.text:
Square the outer and inner functions on $[0, 2]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = \sqrt{x + 2} \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = x + 2$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = 1 \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 1$$

Form the difference and set up the integral:
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x + 2) - 1 = x + 1$$
$$V = \pi \int_0^2 (x + 1) \, dx = \pi \left[\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x\right]_0^2$$

Evaluate at the limits:
$$= \pi \left(\frac{2^2}{2} + 2 - 0\right) = \pi (2 + 2) = 4\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms difference $y_1^2 - y_2^2 = (x + 2) - 1 = x + 1$ and integrates $\pi \left[\frac{1}{2}x^2 + x\right]_0^2$.

domain_and_existence_restrictions: On $1 \le x \le 4$, $y = \sqrt{x} \le 2$, so $y = 2$ is the outer radius.
hints: Identify the outer radius $y_{\text{outer}} = 2$ and inner radius $y_{\text{inner}} = \sqrt{x}$ on $[1, 4]$.
Square each radius: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 4$ and $y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x$, giving $y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 4 - x$.
Set up the integral: $V = \pi \int_1^4 (4 - x) \, dx$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify outer and inner boundaries on $[1, 4]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 2 \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 4$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = \sqrt{x} \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x$$

Form the difference of squares and set up the washer integral:
$$V = \pi \int_1^4 (4 - x) \, dx$$

Find the antiderivative:
$$= \pi \left[4x - \frac{1}{2}x^2\right]_1^4$$

Substitute the limits $x = 4$ and $x = 1$:
$$= \pi \left(\left(4(4) - \frac{4^2}{2}\right) - \left(4(1) - \frac{1^2}{2}\right)\right) = \pi \left((16 - 8) - \left(4 - \frac{1}{2}\right)\right)$$
$$= \pi \left(8 - \frac{7}{2}\right) = \frac{9}{2}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies outer radius $2$ and inner radius $\sqrt{x}$.
Integrates to $4x - \frac{1}{2}x^2$ and applies both limits.

hints: Outer radius is $y_{\text{outer}} = x + 2$ and inner radius is $y_{\text{inner}} = x + 1$.

walkthrough.text:
Square both linear boundary expressions:
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 = (x + 2)^2 = x^2 + 4x + 4$$
$$y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x + 1)^2 = x^2 + 2x + 1$$

Subtract $y_{	ext{inner}}^2$ from $y_{	ext{outer}}^2$:
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x^2 + 4x + 4) - (x^2 + 2x + 1) = 2x + 3$$

Set up and evaluate the definite integral from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^2 (2x + 3) \, dx = \pi \left[x^2 + 3x\right]_0^2$$

Substitute the limits:
$$= \pi \left((2^2 + 3(2)) - 0\right) = \pi (4 + 6) = 10\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies $(x + 2)$ as the outer radius and $(x + 1)$ as the inner radius.
Integrates to $x^2 + 3x$ and evaluates at both limits.

hints: Outer radius is $y_{\text{outer}} = 1$ and inner radius is $y_{\text{inner}} = (x + 1)^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Square the outer and inner boundaries:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 1 \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 1$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = \frac{1}{x + 1} = (x + 1)^{-1} \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x + 1)^{-2}$$

Form the washer integral on $[0, 1]$:
$$V = \pi \int_0^1 \left(1 - (x + 1)^{-2}\right) \, dx$$

Find the antiderivative:
$$= \pi \left[x - \frac{(x + 1)^{-1}}{-1}\right]_0^1 = \pi \left[x + \frac{1}{x + 1}\right]_0^1$$

Substitute the limits $x = 1$ and $x = 0$:
$$= \pi \left(\left(1 + \frac{1}{1 + 1}\right) - \left(0 + \frac{1}{0 + 1}\right)\right) = \pi \left(\left(1 + \frac{1}{2}\right) - 1\right) = \frac{1}{2}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies outer radius $1$ and inner radius $(x + 1)^{-1}$.
Integrates to $x + (x + 1)^{-1}$ and applies both limits.

hints: Outer radius is $y_{\text{outer}} = 3$ and inner radius is $y_{\text{inner}} = \sqrt{x + 1}$.
Square each boundary: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 9$ and $y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x + 1$, giving $y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = 9 - (x + 1) = 8 - x$.
Set up the integral: $V = \pi \int_0^3 (8 - x) \, dx$.

walkthrough.text:
Square the outer and inner boundaries on $[0, 3]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}} = 3 \implies y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 9$$
$$y_{\text{inner}} = \sqrt{x + 1} \implies y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x + 1$$

Form the difference $y_{	ext{outer}}^2 - y_{	ext{inner}}^2$:
$$9 - (x + 1) = 8 - x$$

Set up and evaluate the definite integral:
$$V = \pi \int_0^3 (8 - x) \, dx = \pi \left[8x - \frac{1}{2}x^2\right]_0^3$$

Substitute the limits $x = 3$ and $x = 0$:
$$= \pi \left(\left(8(3) - \frac{3^2}{2}\right) - 0\right) = \pi \left(24 - \frac{9}{2}\right) = \frac{39}{2}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

hints: Split the region into two sections at $x = 1$: section 1 on $[0, 1]$ and section 2 on $[1, 3]$. Inner boundary is $y = 1$ throughout.

walkthrough.text:
Recognize that the upper boundary changes definition at $x = 1$, while the inner radius is $y = 1$ ($y_{	ext{inner}}^2 = 1$) throughout:
$$V = V_1 + V_2 = \pi \int_0^1 \left((x + 2)^2 - 1\right) \, dx + \pi \int_1^3 \left((4 - x)^2 - 1\right) \, dx$$

Evaluate $V_1$ over $[0, 1]$:
$$\text{Integrand } = (x + 2)^2 - 1 = x^2 + 4x + 3$$
$$V_1 = \pi \left[\frac{x^3}{3} + 2x^2 + 3x\right]_0^1 = \pi \left(\frac{1}{3} + 2 + 3\right) = \frac{16}{3}\pi$$

Evaluate $V_2$ over $[1, 3]$:
$$\text{Integrand } = (4 - x)^2 - 1 = x^2 - 8x + 15$$
$$V_2 = \pi \left[\frac{x^3}{3} - 4x^2 + 15x\right]_1^3 = \pi \left((9 - 36 + 45) - \left(\frac{1}{3} - 4 + 15\right)\right)$$
$$= \pi \left(18 - \frac{34}{3}\right) = \frac{20}{3}\pi$$

Add the two volumes together:
$$V = V_1 + V_2 = \frac{16}{3}\pi + \frac{20}{3}\pi = \frac{36}{3}\pi = 12\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Recognises that the radial rule changes at $x = 1$ and uses inner radius $1$ throughout.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires solving for intersection limits, squaring both curves and integrating the polynomial difference.

domain_and_existence_restrictions: Curves intersect at $x = -1$ and $x = 3$; on $[-1, 3]$, $2x + 4 \ge x^2 + 1 \ge 0$.
hints: Find the intersection points by equating equations: $2x + 4 = x^2 + 1 \implies x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = -1, 3$.
On $[-1, 3]$, the line is upper ($y_{\text{outer}} = 2x + 4$) and the parabola is lower ($y_{\text{inner}} = x^2 + 1$).
Square each function: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 = 4x^2 + 16x + 16$ and $y_{\text{inner}}^2 = x^4 + 2x^2 + 1$. Difference: $-x^4 + 2x^2 + 16x + 15$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the intersection limits by solving $2x + 4 = x^2 + 1$:
$$x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = -1, \quad x = 3$$

Square both curves and form the washer difference on $[-1, 3]$:
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 = (2x + 4)^2 = 4x^2 + 16x + 16$$
$$y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (x^2 + 1)^2 = x^4 + 2x^2 + 1$$
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = -x^4 + 2x^2 + 16x + 15$$

Set up and evaluate the definite integral:
$$V = \pi \int_{-1}^3 (-x^4 + 2x^2 + 16x + 15) \, dx = \pi \left[-\frac{x^5}{5} + \frac{2}{3}x^3 + 8x^2 + 15x\right]_{-1}^3$$

Evaluate at the upper and lower limits:
$$\text{At } x = 3: \quad -\frac{243}{5} + 18 + 72 + 45 = 135 - \frac{243}{5} = \frac{432}{5}$$$$\text{At } x = -1: \quad \frac{1}{5} - \frac{2}{3} + 8 - 15 = -7 + \frac{3 - 10}{15} = -\frac{112}{15}$$$$V = \pi \left(\frac{432}{5} - \left(-\frac{112}{15}\right)\right) = \pi \left(\frac{1296 + 112}{15}\right) = \frac{1408}{15}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves $2x + 4 = x^2 + 1$ to obtain the limits $x = -1$ and $x = 3$.
Establishes that $2x + 4$ is the outer radius throughout the interval.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: find irrational surd intersection limits x = 3 ± sqrt(3) by solving quadratic x(6-x) = 6, set up washer difference of line and reciprocal curve, and carry through exact surd arithmetic to reach 8*sqrt(3)*pi.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires exact evaluation of volume of revolution between line and reciprocal curve with irrational limits.

hints: Find the intersection points: $6 - x = \dfrac{6}{x} \implies x^2 - 6x + 6 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 24}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{3}$.
Between the intersections, the line lies above the reciprocal curve: $y_{\text{outer}}^2 - y_{\text{inner}}^2 = (6 - x)^2 - 36x^{-2} = 36 - 12x + x^2 - 36x^{-2}$.

Substitute $b = 3 + \sqrt{3}$ and $a = 3 - \sqrt{3}$ using $b - a = 2\sqrt{3}$, $b^2 - a^2 = 12\sqrt{3}$, $b^3 - a^3 = 60\sqrt{3}$, and $\dfrac{1}{b} - \dfrac{1}{a} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ to obtain $8\sqrt{3}\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the $x$-coordinates of the intersections by solving $6 - x = \dfrac{6}{x}$:
$$x(6 - x) = 6 \implies 6x - x^2 = 6 \implies x^2 - 6x + 6 = 0$$
$$x = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(1)(6)}}{2} = \frac{6 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{3}$$

Square the outer line and inner reciprocal curve:
$$y_{\text{outer}}^2 = (6 - x)^2 = 36 - 12x + x^2$$
$$y_{\text{inner}}^2 = \left(\frac{6}{x}\right)^2 = \frac{36}{x^2} = 36x^{-2}$$
$$\text{Integrand } = 36 - 12x + x^2 - 36x^{-2}$$

Find the indefinite integral:
$$\int (36 - 12x + x^2 - 36x^{-2}) \, dx = 36x - 6x^2 + \frac{1}{3}x^3 + \frac{36}{x}$$

Evaluate the difference between limits $b = 3 + \sqrt{3}$ and $a = 3 - \sqrt{3}$:
$$b - a = 2\sqrt{3}, \quad b^2 - a^2 = 12\sqrt{3}, \quad b^3 - a^3 = 60\sqrt{3}, \quad \frac{1}{b} - \frac{1}{a} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$$$$\Delta = 36(2\sqrt{3}) - 6(12\sqrt{3}) + \frac{1}{3}(60\sqrt{3}) + 36\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)$$$$= 72\sqrt{3} - 72\sqrt{3} + 20\sqrt{3} - 12\sqrt{3} = 8\sqrt{3}$$$$V = 8\sqrt{3}\pi \text{ cubic units}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies $6 - x$ as the outer radius between the intersections.
Substitutes both irrational limits without decimal approximation.
Uses the relations for $3 \pm \sqrt{3}$ or equivalent exact algebra to simplify the difference.
